competition.title: Syntax Strike
competition.details:
Date of Event is 15 October 2026

EVENT GUIDELINES & RULES

1.      General Rules:

  1. This is a pair-based coding competition. Each team must consist of exactly 2 participants.
  2. Both team members must actively participate in the competition.
  3. Participants must have a basic understanding of the Python programming language.
  4. The event will consist of 3 rounds:
    • Round 1: Code & Debug
    • Round 2: Constraint Code
    • Round 3: Code Chase
  5. The total competition duration will be 1 hours and 50 minutes (110 minutes).
  6. Participants must follow the instructions given by the event coordinators and judges.
  7. Participants must complete the competition independently, using only resources explicitly authorized by the event coordinators.
  8. The use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools or AI-assisted services is strictly prohibited. This includes chatbots, code generators, code completion tools, debugging assistants, solution generators, and tools that generate, rewrite, explain, or optimize code or answers.
  9. Participants must not use unauthorized assistance, including copied code, prewritten solutions, online solution repositories, external help from non-team members, or any other resource that provides an unfair advantage.
  10. Participants may be required to explain their code or demonstrate their understanding of the submitted solution. Failure to do so may result in disqualification.
  11. Organizers may inspect devices, software, browser activity, or submitted code when necessary to verify compliance with event rules.
  12. Participants must not bring their own laptops. The required systems will be provided by the organizers.
  13. No Verbal or Written Communication: Participants are strictly prohibited from communicating with their teammates or any other participant during all three rounds.
  14. Participants must work independently on their assigned tasks without verbal assistance, discussion, or exchange of solutions.
  15. Communication with event coordinators or judges is permitted only when necessary to report technical issues or when explicitly authorized.
  16. Any form of unfair practice or misconduct may lead to disqualification.
  17. Swapping between team members are strictly prohibited in round 1 and 2.

2. Round 1: Code & Debug

Duration: 30 Minutes

  1. One participant will be assigned the task of writing code based on a given output.
  2. The other participant will be provided with incorrect code that must be debugged.
  3. Both participants will work on their respective tasks simultaneously.
  4. Both tasks must be completed successfully for the team to qualify for the next round.
  5. Participants must complete their assigned tasks within the allotted 30 minutes.
  6. The submitted code must produce the required output and function correctly within the given time limit.

3. Round 2: Constraint Code

Duration: 30 Minutes

  1. Both participants will be assigned individual coding tasks to complete independently.
  2. Each participant have write code using constrains given by the event coordinator.
  3. Participants may be asked to shorten, optimize, or modify the given code according to the instructions.
  4. Certain programming constructs, functions, or keywords may be restricted during this round. Examples of restrictions include not using while loops, for loops, specific built-in functions, or other constructs specified by the coordinators.
  5. Each participant must ensure that their modified code produces the required output and satisfies all the given constraints.
  6. Participants must not use alternative methods that violate the stated restrictions.
  7. Both participants must complete and submit their respective solutions within the allotted 20 minutes.
  8. Qualification Rule: Both participants must successfully complete their individual tasks to qualify for Round 3. If either participant fails to qualify, the entire team will be eliminated.
  9. Solutions will be evaluated based on correctness, adherence to constraints, code efficiency, and successful execution.
  10. Failure to follow any specified constraint may result in disqualification from the round.

4. Round 3: Code Chase

Duration: 60 Minutes (30 + 30 Minutes)

  1. Each team will be given a problem statement.
  2. The first participant will write the initial part of the solution within 30 minutes.
  3. After the first 30 minutes, the participants must switch roles.
  4. The second participant will continue and complete the code written by the first participant.
  5. The first participant must stop coding immediately when the first 30-minute period ends.
  6. The second participant will get another 30 minutes to complete the solution.
  7. The second participant must continue working based on the existing code and the provided problem statement.
  8. The second participant may modify, correct, or extend the existing code to complete the problem.
  9. The final submission must be made before the total time limit of 60 minutes expires.
  10. The first participant can not use comment as a hint for their team member.

5. Evaluation Criteria

The performance of participants will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

  1. Code Correctness: Whether the submitted code produces the expected output.
  2. Test Cases Passed: The number of test cases successfully passed by the submitted solution.
  3. Problem Understanding: How accurately the solution addresses the given problem statement.
  4. Adherence to Constraints: Whether all specified restrictions are followed in the Constraint Code round.
  5. Code Efficiency: The logical implementation and appropriate use of programming constructs.
  6. Handling of Edge Cases: The ability of the code to handle boundary inputs.
  7. Time Management: Completion and submission of tasks within the allotted time.
  8. Team Participation: Active involvement of both team members throughout the competition.
  9. Rule Compliance: Adherence to all event rules and restrictions.
  1. Disqualification Rules

A team may be disqualified for any of the following reasons:

  1. Using unauthorized resources or external assistance.
  2. Using AI tools or AI-assisted services, including chatbots, code generators, debugging tools, code completion tools, or solution generators.
  3. Submitting code copied from another source or generated or substantially modified by an AI system or an unauthorized person.
  4. Sharing code or solutions with other teams.
  5. Attempting to bypass event rules, restrictions, monitoring, or device checks.
  6. Using unauthorized software, websites, plugins, extensions, or external communication channels.
  7. Violating the specific restrictions given in the Constraint Code round.
  8. Engaging in unauthorized verbal or written communication with teammates or other participants during the competition.
  9. Interfering with another team’s work or receiving unauthorized assistance during restricted periods.
  10. Misconduct or failure to follow the instructions of the coordinators or judges.
  11. Failing to submit the solution within the allotted time.
  12. Being unable to explain or demonstrate an understanding of the submitted code when requested by the judges.
  13. Using comment as a hint for their team member.
  14. Bringing or using unauthorized personal devices or equipment during the competition.

7. Final Decision

  1. The judges’ decision will be final and binding.
  2. Only teams that successfully qualify through the required rounds will be eligible for the final round.
  3. The organizers reserve the right to verify compliance with event rules at any stage of the competition.
  4. The organizers reserve the right to modify the event rules if necessary, with appropriate notice to participants.
  5. Any issue not covered in these guidelines will be resolved by the event coordinators and judges.
